embed:rst The `KVP`_ key that overrides the resource the `section`_ itself matched :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A texture-only recolour is written with it -- ``hash`` names one of the game's textures and ``this`` names what to draw in its place -- so a `section`_ carrying it binds no register of its own

briefdescription.para: The starting prefix used for some section_ that overrides a mod's shader.
The substring used to indicate a section_ is edited by this software.

para.verbatim: embed:rst The substring that usually occurs in the name of a `section`_ to indicate that the `section`_ will call some ``*.Blend.buf`` file
embed:rst The substring that usually occurs in the name of a `section`_ to indicate that the `section`_ will call some ``*.Position.buf`` file
embed:rst The substring that usually occurs in the name of a `section`_ to indicate that the `section`_ will call some ``*.Texcoord.buf`` file

briefdescription.para: The substring used to indicate that the section_ was created by this program.

para.verbatim: embed:rst The substring used to indicate that the `section`_ contains some edited/created texture ``*.RemapTex.dds`` file

briefdescription.para: The substring used to indicate that the section_ contains some downloaded file from the internet.

para.verbatim:
embed:rst The substring used to indicate that a resource `section`_ INSIDE a fix's block names a file the fix did **not** write -- one of the mod's own, referenced by the fix :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` An undo takes every section of the fix's block out and deletes every file those sections name, which is right for a ``RemapBlend`` / ``RemapTex`` / ``RemapDL`` file the fix produced and destroys the mod for a texture the fix merely bound (the WWMI fixer binds a mod's textures by register, and a file no resource of the mod's own ``.ini`` names has to be declared somewhere). A section carrying this keyword is removed with the block and its file is left alone -- see :cpp:func:`RemapIniRemover::collectRemovedResources`

briefdescription.para: The KVP_ key used to reference/call another section_.

para.verbatim: embed:rst The `KVP`_ key holding a `section`_'s model hash -- what :cpp:class:`GIMISectionClassifier` looks a mod object up by

embed:rst The `KVP`_ key holding the first index of the model a `section`_ draws -- the second half of what :cpp:class:`GIMISectionClassifier` looks a mod object up by, for the mod objects a ``hash`` alone cannot tell apart
embed:rst The `KVP`_ key holding how many indices of the model a `section`_ draws
embed:rst The `KVP`_ key holding how many vertices the model a `section`_ draws has
embed:rst The `KVP`_ key breaking the tie when several `sections`_ match one draw

briefdescription.para: The filter_index KVP_ key the value a shader's own draw writes into IniConstants, which a remapped section_ matches on to tell one pass from another.
The array KVP_ key how many elements a buffer resource holds.

para.verbatim: embed:rst The `KVP`_ key holding which kind of draw call a `section`_ matches

memberdef.name: MatchKeys
memberdef.initializer: = { Hash, MatchPriority, MatchFirstIndex, MatchIndexCount, MatchType, MatchVertexCount}

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Every `KVP`_ key by which a `section`_ selects the draw it overrides :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` These are what make a ``TextureOverride`` fire, so they are meaningful only where 3dmigoto is matching. A ``CommandList`` is *called*, never matched, so a fix that copies a section's body into one drops these on the way -- carried across they say nothing, and a stale ``hash`` in particular reads as a second claim on a draw the fix has already remapped

embed:rst The `KVP`_ key naming the file a resource `section`_ points at :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. note:: Classes that edit `KVPs`_ generically take this as a ``K``-typed customization point instead (eg. :cpp:type:`BaseResEdit::ResEditConfig`'s ``filenameKey``), since ``K`` is not ``std::string`` in the `pybind11`_ layer. This constant is for the plain-``std::string`` callers, and for keeping the one spelling in one place

embed:rst The prefix a register binding uses to name a resource `section`_ rather than a value -- ``ps-t0 = ref ResourceFoo``. Strip it with :cpp:func:`IniNamingTools::removeRefPrefix` rather than by hand: it was written out at seven sites across three files, one of them carrying the literal's LENGTH as a bare 4
embed:rst A resource `section`_'s kind, eg. ``type = Buffer``
embed:rst A resource `section`_'s bytes per element, eg. ``stride = 40``
embed:rst A resource `section`_'s element format, eg. ``format = R32_UINT``
embed:rst The value a `KVP`_ carries to mean "nothing at all" -- a ``filename =`` naming this is a placeholder, not a real resource
embed:rst The statement that fills a resource with a copy of another: ``ResourceX = copy ResourceY``
embed:rst The statement that gives a resource another's description only: ``ResourceX = copy_desc ResourceY``
embed:rst The `KVP`_ key naming a `section`_'s index buffer -- also the last index column of the :cpp:class:`Hashes` row holding that buffer's hash

briefdescription.para: The KVP_ key naming a section_'s position vertex buffer.

para.verbatim: embed:rst The `KVP`_ key naming a `section`_'s blend **or** texcoord vertex buffer -- which of the two it is depends on the `section`_, not on the key
embed:rst The `KVP`_ key controlling how a draw call is handled -- ``skip`` is the only value this software writes, alongside \ref Draw, after a downloaded ``Blend.buf``
embed:rst The `KVP`_ key issuing a non-indexed draw, written as ``<vertex count>,0`` -- the pair \ref Handling completes after a downloaded ``Blend.buf``
embed:rst The `KVP`_ key that actually draws a model. What a texture fix has to be issued in front of -- see :cpp:class:`RegDelimitedAdd`

embed:rst The sub-command call to `ORFix`_ (Outline Reflection Fix) :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` One of the two fixes shipped by an external ``3dmigoto`` library that work around textures the game breaks each version. A ``run =`` naming this is a call into that library, not into the mod's own `sections`_

embed:rst The sub-command call to ``NNFix`` (No Normal Fix) -- the other half of the same external library as \ref ORFixPath :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` .. note:: It lives under the library's ``ORFix`` folder, **not** an ``NNFix`` one. That asymmetry is the library's, not a typo here

embed:rst GIMI's own texture helper, ``CommandList\GIMI\SetTextures`` -- ORFix reading :cpp:member:`GIMINormalMap` / :cpp:member:`GIMIDiffuse` / :cpp:member:`GIMILightMap` instead of ``ps-t0`` / ``ps-t1`` / ``ps-t2``. A mod's use of it is rewritten into the traditional API as it is read -- see :cpp:class:`GIMIApiNormalizer`

briefdescription.para: The normal map key of GIMI's texture API read as ps-t0, see GIMISetTexturesPath.
The diffuse key of GIMI's texture API read as ps-t1, see GIMISetTexturesPath.
The light map key of GIMI's texture API read as ps-t2, see GIMISetTexturesPath.

para.verbatim:
embed:rst The folder holding the `TexFx`_ external library's sub-commands :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A third addon alongside ORFix and NNFix, and the one that gives textures capabilities the importer does not have on its own -- most visibly making parts of a model look transparent. What each channel of an input texture means is documented on its own GitHub rather than here :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` It owns **two dedicated registers**, ``ps-t69`` and ``ps-t70``, which is why a fix that shifts a character's registers around leaves those two alone

embed:rst The first of `TexFx`_'s two dedicated registers :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A modder opts into TexFx by binding these, which is what makes the library optional where NNFix and ORFix are mandatory -- so a fix issues a TexFx sub-command only where one of them is actually bound, never simply because the character's row names one
embed:rst `TexFx`_'s variable that, at ``-1``, makes it leave a draw to the game's own shader

briefdescription.para: The second of TexFx_'s two dedicated registers see PsT69.

para.verbatim:
embed:rst `TexFx`_'s transparency sub-command for a diffuse living on ``ps-t0``, GI 5.0 and later :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The call names the register the diffuse is on, so which of these two a fix issues follows from where its register shift left the diffuse -- not from the character
embed:rst `TexFx`_'s transparency sub-command for a diffuse living on ``ps-t1`` -- see \ref TexFxTransparency0

embed:rst The PRE-5.0 spelling of \ref TexFxTransparency0 -- ``T.0`` rather than ``TN.0`` :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` The same sub-command, which `TexFx`_ itself renamed at 5.0. A fix transcribed from a 4.x row has to issue THIS one: the two are not interchangeable, and issuing the 5.0 name names a sub-command that library does not have -- which surfaces as an effect that quietly does nothing rather than as an error
embed:rst The PRE-5.0 spelling of \ref TexFxTransparency1 -- see \ref TexFxTransparency0Pre5_0
embed:rst Written in place of a ``hash`` that has no mapping onto the mod being fixed to -- see :cpp:class:`RegAssetRemap`
embed:rst Written in place of a ``match_first_index`` that has no mapping onto the mod being fixed to -- the index counterpart of :cpp:member:`HashNotFound`

embed:rst A WWMI Tools export's shape-key vertex offsets -- see :cpp:class:`WWMIShapeKeys`
